title: Permission test harness: golden fixtures + CI regression suite for RBAC v2
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a deterministic, reviewable permission testing harness for RBAC v2 that uses golden fixtures to validate permission evaluation logic, ensures audit logging contains the correct decision metadata, and is integrated into CI as a nightly regression suite to catch permission regressions early. This ticket covers designing the harness, authoring initial golden fixtures for common and edge-case roles, SSO/SAML token simulation strategies, audit-log assertions, and CI orchestration.

Background:
RBAC v2 introduces a richer permission model (scopes, resource-anchored grants, inheritance, conditional rules). Without an automated, repeatable test corpus we keep seeing intermittent regressions in policy evaluation when we introduce kernel/runtime optimizations and microservice refactors. We also need to validate that audit logs capture both the evaluated policy and the pre/post decision context required by compliance teams.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
- A test harness that can load golden fixtures and run permission evaluation against the RBAC v2 engine in both local dev and CI environments.
- Golden fixtures cover: baseline roles (admin, viewer, operator), composite roles (team+project scoped), explicit denies, conditional rules (timebound, IP-based), and inheritance/overrides.
- Simulated SSO/SAML assertions can be injected to exercise subject attributes (groups, claims, external_id).
- End-to-end assertions include: evaluation result (allow/deny), matched policy ID, policy version, and resulting audit log entries with required fields (actor, resource, action, decision_reason, policy_snapshot).
- Tests run in CI nightly and block merges if new failures are detected for a P0/P1 regression.
- Documentation and a small guide for engineers to add new fixtures.

Proposed Approach:
1) Harness: Build on top of existing test runner (pytest) with a permission_test_cli wrapper. The wrapper takes a fixture file and executes evaluations against a local instance of the policy service or a test double of the evaluator. Output is normalized JSON to compare against golden file.
2) Golden Fixtures: YAML-based fixtures in test/fixtures/rbac_v2/golden/. Each fixture contains: description, input (subject metadata, resource metadata, action, context), expected evaluation (allow/deny, matched_policy, explanations), and expected audit_log fragment.
3) SSO/SAML Simulation: Use a token factory in tests that emits JWTs with mimicked SAML attributes (i.e., urn:claim:saml:groups). For full SAML assertion tests we will run a lightweight test IdP container (mitreid-connect or local SAML simulator) in CI for one integration test job.
4) Audit Log Validation: Instrument the test harness to tail the test audit sink (local file or ephemeral DB). Assertions validate required audit fields and a hash match of the policy_snapshot to ensure no silent policy drift.
5) Regression Suite: Add a dedicated pipeline job (nightly-rbac-regressions). Failures triage flow: failures create an automated issue in Linear with prefilled diagnostics and links to failing fixture and PR.

Fixture examples (conceptual):
- fixture-0001-admin-allow.yaml: admin role, write action, expect allow, matched_policy: admin-full-access, audit_log contains decision_reason:"role:admin"
- fixture-0014-explicit-deny.yaml: operator role with explicit deny for delete, expect deny, matched_policy: deny-delete-ops, audit log includes policy_snapshot hash and actor attributes
- fixture-0022-timebound-access.yaml: project-contractor role with current_time outside allowed window -> deny + audit reason: "condition:time-window"

CI/Automation Details:
- Unit tests run on every PR. Golden-regression job runs nightly against the main branch and a pinned baseline of policy definitions (policy-bundle@mainhash).
- When the policy-bundle or engine changes, a 'golden refresh' workflow will run to propose updated golden fixtures with diffs. Changes require explicit approval from Security and Product (via REVIEW labels) before being committed.
- Provide a small dashboard (Grafana) showing regression trend (failures by fixture, last changed, last passing build).

Implementation notes & trade-offs:
- We prefer golden fixtures to property-based testing for auditability and human reviewability. Property tests may be added later for fuzzing edge cases.
- Running a SAML IdP in CI increases complexity but provides higher fidelity; we will scope it to a single nightly integration test to limit flakiness.
- To avoid flakiness from time-dependent rules, fixtures will include a deterministic "clock" override field and CI job will run with a fixed TIME env var unless specifically testing time-based logic.

Security & Compliance:
- Audit logs used in tests must be scrubbed of PII. Fixtures should use synthetic IDs and synthetic user attributes.
- Tests asserting KMS/HSM encryption of audit logs will be mocked; full encryption pipeline verification delegated to an ops integration test separate from this suite.

Docs & Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Golden+Fixtures+Design
- Draft PR (initial harness): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2487 (WIP)
- Fixture repo path: tests/fixtures/rbac_v2/golden/

Next steps / Implementation plan:
- (Day 0-2) Finalize fixture schema and create 12 starter fixtures (Maya/Alexei).
- (Day 3-5) Implement permission_test_cli and local audit sink; land basic harness PR.
- (Day 6-10) Add SSO token factory and 3 SAML integration fixtures; add CI nightly job.
- (Day 11-14) Run 2-week stabilization, address flaky fixtures, add docs and examples.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Golden fixtures will need frequent updates when policy semantics change. Mitigation: golden-refresh bot and approval gate.
- Risk: CI flakiness due to external simulators (SAML, DB). Mitigation: limit integration to one nightly job, use container health checks and retries.

Estimated effort: 5 story points (2 devs, ~2 weeks including validation and docs).
